subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI plain-text accessibility setting, and what public config key/default/replacement semantics should it use?
rationale: The source paths are clear, but this adds durable public config behavior and accessibility UX semantics that automation should not decide without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add bounded TUI plain-text mode
options.body: Implement an optional core TUI setting with ASCII replacements across tool display, selectors, docs, schema, and tests while preserving current rich output by default.

options.title: Defer the config surface
options.body: Keep the issue open as a product backlog item until maintainers decide the naming and replacement semantics.

options.title: Reject core config for now
options.body: Close only if maintainers explicitly decide that TUI glyph suppression is not a core product direction despite the screen-reader reports.

recommendation.title: Add bounded TUI plain-text mode
recommendation.body: Implement an optional core TUI setting with ASCII replacements across tool display, selectors, docs, schema, and tests while preserving current rich output by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history points to steipete for original TUI/tool-display ownership and current config/TUI review context.
